titel: The business model of the financial industry
kurz: Which parties earn money from a securities account, from which sources, and why the form of remuneration determines the recommendation.

bloecke.md:
A financial product has two prices. One appears on the contract note; the other pays the parties behind it: fund management company, depositary, index provider, trading venue, broker and intermediary. This second price is usually the larger one. It is designed so that it never appears as an invoice. The investor notices it only as a slightly lower return.

These costs are justified in principle, because custody, liquidity, settlement and distribution are real services that cost money. A conflict of interest arises where the way payment is made decides which product is recommended. Assessing the industry therefore starts with the question of whom a product pays, and only then with the question of what it costs.

## The parties and their income

It starts with the fund management company (Kapitalverwaltungsgesellschaft). It launches the fund and takes its management fee daily, pro rata, from the [[Segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen)|segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen)]]. The investor does not transfer this fee; it shows only in a marginally lower unit price. The [[TER]] sums up this ongoing deduction. From it the company also pays the depositary, which holds the securities and checks the fund's accounting, as well as the licence for the index the fund tracks. A second income arises from the client assets themselves, namely through [[Securities lending|securities lending]]. At iShares, 62.5% of lending income goes into the fund assets and the provider keeps 37.5%.

The broker earns from order fees, from trading venue fees passed on to clients, from the foreign currency mark-up on US securities and from interest on securities-backed loans. In addition there is the interest margin, that is the difference between what the uninvested balance earns on the money market and the part of it that is credited to the settlement account.

Some trading venues earn nothing at all from fees. On gettex, neither a brokerage fee (Courtage) nor an exchange fee is charged. Trading there is provided by Baader Bank as the sole [[Market maker|market maker]]; on LS Exchange, Lang & Schwarz takes on this role. In these cases the income comes from the difference between bid and ask price, the [[Spread|spread]], and is therefore contained in the price rather than shown on the contract note. The boundaries between the parties are also blurred. Deutsche Börse holds 42.84% of Tradegate Exchange, and Tradegate AG holds the same share. The reference exchange and a competing exchange are thus linked through shareholdings.

A fund is sold with a 5% initial charge on the unit price. With an investment amount of €10,500, €500 goes to the sales channel and €10,000 is invested.

A broad index ETF with ongoing charges of 0.20% costs around €20 a year on €10,000. The initial charge therefore equals 25 years of ongoing charges. It is paid all at once on purchase, that is before the first euro of return has been earned.

## Legal separation of commission and fee

In Germany both models exist side by side, governed by separate provisions.

Independent intermediaries work under Section 34f GewO (Trade Regulation Act). They arrange investment funds and capital investments (Vermögensanlagen), are paid by the product provider and are supervised by the trade authorities. Their counterpart is the fee-based financial investment adviser (Honorar-Finanzanlagenberater) under Section 34h GewO. This adviser is paid by the client, may not keep any commissions and must pass them on to the client. In insurance, the same dividing line runs between the intermediary under Section 34d(1) GewO and the insurance consultant (Versicherungsberater) under Section 34d(2) GewO.

For banks and investment firms, the WpHG (Securities Trading Act) applies. Inducements from third parties, the collective term for commissions of every kind, are permitted under Section 70 WpHG only if they improve the quality of the service and are disclosed. Under Section 63(7) WpHG, the total cost must be disclosed before the transaction and annually afterwards, in euros and as a percentage and including inducements. Under Section 64(1) WpHG, the firm must also state in advance whether it provides the advice as independent fee-based investment advice (Honorar-Anlageberatung). Disclosure is thus largely regulated. The conflict of interest nonetheless remains, because disclosure does not abolish the commissions.

bloecke.titel: Four forms of remuneration and their incentives
bloecke.unter: The conflict of interest is created by tying remuneration to a sale, regardless of its amount.

felder.text: Commission-free policy or net tariff, remuneration agreed separately. The product contains no acquisition costs; the service is paid for separately and is negotiable.
Initial charge, acquisition commission. Revenue arises only when something is signed. Sales therefore need occasions.
Section 34h GewO, consumer advice centres, hourly or flat fee. The advice to change nothing is paid for here just like any other.
Flows as long as the product stays in place. Rewards holding rather than switching, but depends on volume, regardless of the quality of the advice.

bloecke.md:
In unit-linked life and pension insurance, the acquisition and distribution costs are subject to Zillmer adjustment (Zillmerung), that is they are offset in advance against the first premiums. Section 169(3) VVG (Insurance Contract Act) sets a limit. Under it, the surrender value must be at least the amount that results when these costs are spread over the first five years. For accounting purposes, since 2015 under the Life Insurance Reform Act (Lebensversicherungsreformgesetz) of 2014, at most 25 per mille of the total premiums may be offset in this way; previously it was 40. In addition, Section 49 VAG (Insurance Supervision Act) requires a commission clawback period (Stornohaftungszeit) of at least five years, during which the commission must be repaid pro rata if the policy is surrendered.

Policyholders who surrender a unit-linked policy after three years therefore often get back considerably less than they paid in. This applies even if the funds within the policy have risen.

## Effect of costs in the portfolio

Costs reduce the final value, including the interest that the deducted amounts would have earned over the entire term. The monthly contribution is unaffected. The following illustrative calculation assumes €250 a month over 25 years and a 6% gross return before costs. A total of €75,000 is paid in.

bloecke.md:
A cross-check shows how much of this reaches the sales side. Over the term, around €3,570 of the initial charge goes to the sales channel. If a trail commission of 0.4% a year on the respective portfolio value is also paid, it adds up to around €5,150 in the same model. Together that is about €8,700 for advice for which the client never saw an invoice. At an hourly rate of €200, this would equal more than 40 hours of advice spread over 25 years. During that time most investors speak to their intermediary barely a dozen times.

Part of the damage, however, is borne by the tax authorities, because lost gains are not taxed either. For an equity fund, the [[Partial exemption (Teilfreistellung)|partial exemption (Teilfreistellung)]] of 30% under Section 20 InvStG (Investment Tax Act) applies. The remainder is subject to the [[Flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer)|flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer)]] of 25% plus solidarity surcharge (Section 32d EStG, Income Tax Act), which together comes to an effective rate of around 18.5%. After tax, the gross loss of €46,219 thus falls to roughly €37,700. This does not change the order of magnitude.

## Sales incentives and product selection

Intermediaries whose income depends on a sale need occasions for sales. A broadly diversified global portfolio, an occupational disability insurance policy and an instant-access savings account offer a single occasion and then none for decades. A thematic fund, a bonus certificate or a portfolio switch, by contrast, offer new occasions again and again.

This is rarely intentional; mostly it is a selection effect. Products with a margin finance sales, training, advertising and comparison portals. Products without a margin lack this support. That is why you hear a lot about the former and little about the latter. The reason is the remuneration rather than the quality, because nobody earns money by pointing to a product without a margin.

On the other hand, commission-based sales reach people who would never pay a fee for advice, and poor protection costs more than any commission. Fee-based advice costs visible money, rarely pays off for small sums and does not guarantee better answers. The form of remuneration says something about the incentives, but not everything about the quality of the advice.

schritte.titel: Ask for the remuneration in euros, one-off and ongoing
schritte.text: What you want is an amount in euros, not a percentage and not a sentence like “the company covers that”. The right to this figure is set out in Section 63(7) WpHG. If the adviser cannot or will not name the figure promptly, that is a warning sign.

schritte.titel: Ask about the rejected alternative and its costs
schritte.text: A sound recommendation includes a benchmark for comparison. If there is no comparison with a simple option, such as a broad index fund or an instant-access savings account, no alternatives were weighed and the product was merely sold.

schritte.titel: Ask about the remuneration if you cancel after three years
schritte.text: This question separates acquisition remuneration from trail remuneration and makes the commission clawback visible. It also shows how long the product must be held for it to pay off for the investor.

bloecke.md:
Payment for order flow (PFOF), the rebate a trading venue pays the broker for routing client orders to it, has been banned in the EU since 28 March 2024 by Article 39a MiFIR (Regulation (EU) 2024/791). Germany made use of the transitional option. For German brokers, PFOF ended on 30 June 2026.

This removes the conflict of interest in order execution. The brokers' need for revenue remains, however, and shifts to order fees, spreads, interest margins and subscription models. With every regulation of this kind, when one source of income disappears, another one grows. Investors should therefore reread their brokers' price lists in 2026 instead of hoping for prices to fall automatically.

In parallel, the EU negotiated the Retail Investment Strategy from 2023 onwards. A more far-reaching ban on commissions was one of the main points of contention. The provisional agreement between Parliament and Council of 18 December 2025 does without such a ban and instead introduces an additional test for inducements. The final votes are scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2026.

The question “What does this cost me?” is not enough on its own. More revealing is the question of who is paid for proposing this particular product, and from which money. In Germany there is a duty to provide information on both, and for securities transactions also a duty of disclosure before the transaction.

mitnehmen: Fund management company, depositary, index provider, broker, trading venue and intermediary are all paid from the same source: the investor's assets.
The conflict of interest arises from tying remuneration to a sale, regardless of its amount.
With €75,000 paid in, ongoing charges of 1.90% plus a 5% initial charge reduce the final value in the model by around €46,000 over 25 years.
The disclosure obligations under Section 63(7) and Section 70 WpHG do not eliminate the conflict; they merely make it recognisable.
If a source of revenue is banned, as PFOF was with effect from 30 June 2026, the need for revenue remains and shifts to other fees and margins.

begriffe.text: Ongoing remuneration that a fund management company passes on from its management fee to the custodian or the intermediary for as long as the fund unit remains in the portfolio. It does not depend on a sale. Its amount depends on the volume rather than on the quality of the advice.

Collective term in the WpHG for commissions, fees and benefits in kind that an investment services firm receives from third parties. Under Section 70 WpHG, inducements are permitted only if they improve the quality of the service and are disclosed to the client.

One-off surcharge on the unit price when buying an investment fund, typically up to around 5%. It goes to the sales channel and immediately reduces the amount invested. For an ETF with ongoing charges of 0.20%, a 5% initial charge equals around 25 years of TER.

Offsetting of the acquisition and distribution costs of a life or pension insurance policy against the first premiums. For the surrender value, Section 169(3) VVG requires these costs to be spread over at least five years. For accounting purposes, a maximum rate of 25 per mille of the total premiums has applied since 2015 under the LVRG (Life Insurance Reform Act) of 2014.

Form of advice in which only the client pays and inducements from third parties are passed on to the client. The legal bases are Section 64 WpHG for investment firms and Section 34h GewO for independent fee-based financial investment advisers (Honorar-Finanzanlagenberater).
